2	
3	Edits made by a session are reviewable as diffs, in the transcript and in the editor.
4

8	- Pre-edit content is captured by the extension at permission time, not by the engine, so it works on both engines.

1	# Agent definition
2	
3	## Why
4	
5	Blind planning exists because a planner that can read the code inherits the code's mistakes as constraints. Every workaround becomes an implicit requirement, and the feature gets shaped to fit the defect. Deriving the spec from intent alone makes disagreement between intent and implementation visible rather than silently absorbed. Phase 2 is not "soften the spec until it fits"; it is "name each disagreement and rule on it", with the code as the presumed-wrong party.
6	
7	## Engines
8	
9	A session runs on one engine, chosen per session or per phase:
10	
11	- Claude through the Agent SDK (Claude Code as a library, JavaScript build, inherited Claude Code login).
12	- GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi K3 through Berget AI (OpenAI-compatible) with our own loop and tools.
13	
14	The extension only sees `CodeSession`: send a prompt, stream events, answer permission requests, interrupt. Engines differ below that line.
15	
16	## Shape
17	
18	Three phases, each a separate session with its own system prompt and tool set. Handoff is files on disk, never conversation context. Planning produces one document, the spec, approved once; reconcile is part of planning and writes its findings into that document.
19	
20	```
21	docs/intent/**  +  work item  →  spec.md  →  spec.md + findings  →  approved spec  →  code
22	                    (blind)                  (reconcile)                            (implement)
23	```
24	
25	## Phase 1: Blind plan
26	
27	Sees: feature description, domain brief (ubiquitous language, stack, constraints), `docs/intent/**`, one work item closure when ADO is connected.
28	Never sees: source, descriptive docs, PRs, build output.
29	
30	Until ADO is connected the feature description is typed by the user or picked from `docs/intent/**`. The agent plans the user story itself; the spec's task list is the source for the ADO tasks created under the story once ADO is connected (write-back, not read-only).
31	
32	Tools: Read/Glob scoped to `docs/intent/**`, `get_work_item(id)`, AskUserQuestion, optionally WebSearch. Bash denied by bare name (allow-lists only auto-approve; a bare-name deny removes the tool from context).
33	
34	First a direction in chat (the decisions that shape the feature, the questions that would change them); nothing is written until the user says go. Then `plan/<feature>.spec.md`: goal and behaviour always, edge cases, tasks and open questions when the feature has them, stable item IDs. To the point, not complete: an item earns its place by changing what gets built or how it is tested. No file paths. If `docs/intent/**` has nothing on the feature, ask and stop.
35	
36	### get_work_item
37	
38	Hand-coded, read-only, Azure DevOps. Server-side filtering is the enforcement.
39	
40	- Include: title, description, parent chain, Goal/Actor/Impact/Behaviour/Example.
41	- Exclude: state, comments, tasks, linked PRs/commits/branches/builds, `System.*` and `Microsoft.VSTS.*` fields.
42	- Walks parents, children, related. Depth and total caps, cycle detection, deterministic ordering. Returns markdown. Snapshot to `plan/<feature>.context.md`.
43	- State is excluded deliberately: a Done item over drifted code is evidence for phase 2, not input to phase 1.
44	- Prose may leak file paths; accepted, or stripped in the tool.
45	
46	### Docs split
47	
48	`docs/intent/**` is phase 1 scope. Everything else is phase 2 only. Descriptive docs drift with the code in the same direction and arrive labelled as authority.
49	
50	## Phase 2: Reconcile
51	
52	Tools: Read, Glob, Grep. Edit/Write/Bash denied by bare name.
53	Input: spec + context + repo. Not the phase 1 transcript.
54	
55	The job is to find what stands in the feature's way before implementation starts, not to grade the spec. Only findings are reported; a spec item the code accommodates without incident is not mentioned. An empty list is a valid result.
56	
57	A finding is one of:
58	
59	| finding | meaning |
60	|---|---|
61	| contradiction | a business rule in the code says otherwise; human decides which side is right |
62	| breakage | existing behaviour the feature would change or break, that the spec does not mention |
63	| naive | the spec assumes something the code shows to be wrong; amend the spec, reason required |
64	
65	Output: a `Findings` section written into the spec, each finding naming the spec item and the code it rests on, short enough to read in one sitting. The user rules on findings as on any other plan item, in the plan session, which revises the spec per ruling and marks the finding resolved; the spec is approved once. Reconcile is started by the user from the plan bar while the spec is a draft, its own session on the plan profile. No separate plan document, no file list: phase 3 finds its files itself.
66	
67	Authority order is fixed in the prompt: work item, then intent doc, then code. Amendments (`naive`) and contradictions ruled in the spec's favour are written back to `docs/intent/**` or the work item as an explicit output, so intent does not rot.
68	
69	## Retrieval
70	
71	A sub-session the planner calls with `retrieve(question, known, budget)` to keep file dumps out of its own context. Phase 2 first; phase 1 only when the intent tree or work-item graph outgrows the planner.
72	
73	- Locates and quotes, never interprets. Output is verbatim excerpts with provenance; the planner rules on them. A summary drops nuance silently, and the planner never sees what was left out.
74	- Tools are derived, not configured: the calling phase's tool set minus AskUserQuestion and anything that writes. Phase 1 retrieval is blind by construction.
75	- No user interaction, no recursion. "Needs X to answer" goes in `not_found`; the planner decides whether to ask. Depth 1.
76	- Result: `findings[]` (excerpt, source as `path#heading`, work item id or URL, one line on why it matches), `not_found[]` (what was looked for, where), `status: complete | partial | budget_exhausted`. Partial is a result, not an error.
77	- Written to `.agent/runs/<id>/retrieval/<n>.md`; the tool returns path, status and counts. Files on disk, not conversation context.
78	- Budget per call (tool calls, tokens), set by the planner. Exhaustion returns findings so far.
79	- Runs as a `CodeSession` under its own profile; a cheap model is fine because the task is search.
80	- Independent questions fan out as independent sessions, no shared state.
81	
82	## Phase 3: Implement
83	
84	Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash. Input is the approved spec only, fresh session started from the plan bar; refuses to start on `status: draft`. Breakage findings the user chose to fix are work items alongside the spec's tasks. Writes go through the ordinary permission prompt; no scope guard.
85	
86	- Task state is the spec: the implementer appends `[done]` or `[blocked: reason]` to a task line, so item 4 of 7 survives a fresh session and shows in the plan view.
87	- Verification on stop through the `kiwiAgent.verify` rules, switchable per session, with the failure budget from settings.
88	- Done when the tests for the behaviours pass, not when the model stops.
89	
90	Parked: build scoped to the project owning the edited file; read-before-edit staleness enforced in a hook rather than by prompt.
91	
92	## Instructions
93	
94	Small shared core plus a per-phase file. Per-type rules inject via PreToolUse hook matched on the path at edit time.
95	
96	- Checkable rules (no `#region`, no AutoMapper/MediatR, nullable on, no `Any`) go to analyzers, `.editorconfig`, BannedApiAnalyzers, grep in the verification hook.
97	- Judgment rules (rule of three, earned abstraction) go to the prompt.
98	- A phase file over a page means the excess is checkable or is spec. Remove alternatives instead of instructing tool preference.
99	
100	### Skills
101	
102	`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and `.agent/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, Claude Code's layout, so one skill serves both engines; `.agent/skills` wins on a shared name. The index (name and description from the frontmatter) rides in the `Skill` tool's description; the model loads a skill itself when a task matches, and the tool returns the body with the skill's folder for relative paths. Phases 2 and 3 and chat carry the tool; the blind planner does not, since skills describe how code is written.
103	
104	## Coordination
105	
106	Claim registry `.agent/sessions/<id>.json`: claimed files, `plan_item_id`, `deadline` set by the session, heartbeat. PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write claims on first touch, denies if another live session holds the file and names who.
107	
108	- Session reports completion and releases the claim. Silence past `deadline` is the stale signal.
109	- Stale claims are flagged in the UI, never auto-released.
110	- Force-release posts a revocation message into the session. The session stops immediately, does not finish the in-flight edit, reports touched files.
111	
112	Checkpoints, opt-in: `checkpoint(reason)` scoped to files under the session's claims; `revert` hash-compares and refuses files that moved underneath. No git. Repeated checkpoints on one plan item mean the item was underspecified; log the reasons.
113	
114	Channels, non-blocking: `send(session, text)` returns immediately; notification is a one-line tail on the receiver's next tool result; `read_messages()` pulls the payload. Registry before channels. Cap thread length and escalate to the user.
115	
116	## Observability
117	
118	Run id, per-phase transcript, tool calls, token spend, checkpoint reasons under `.agent/runs/<id>/`.
119	
120	## Per-phase model
121	
122	Phase 1 wants the strongest reasoner, phase 3 wants throughput. Profiles carry engine, model and effort.
123	
124	## Parked
125	
126	- ADO: `get_work_item` and creating tasks under the user story from the spec's task list. No work items exist yet.
127	- Repo map for phases 2 and 3 (project list, public type index, folder conventions).
128	- Anthropic Messages API adapter under API key in the own-loop engine.
129	- Compaction in the own-loop engine.
130	- Retrieval in phase 1 (large intent tree, work-item graph, WebSearch).
131

1	# KiwiAgent
2	
3	VS Code extension that runs coding sessions with a choice of engine per session.
4	
5	- **Claude**: the Agent SDK's JavaScript build of Claude Code (`dist/cli.mjs`), spawned under Node with the login Claude Code already has. No native binary.
6	- **GLM-5.3-Flash / Kimi K3** through Berget AI (OpenAI-compatible): own loop with Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep and Bash. Read-only tools run without asking; the rest prompt, with "always allow" per tool and session. Needs an API key: run *KiwiAgent: Set API Key for Profile*.
7	
8	The three-phase design (blind plan, reconcile, implement) is the goal; `docs/intent/agent.md` is the definition.
9	
10	The sidebar has a Sessions view (every session, with status) and the Chat view: tabs for the sessions in play with a status icon (📐 planning, 🔧 implementing, 🧪 verifying, ✋ needs you, ⚠ error, ○ waiting), a `+` tab that opens the new-session screen, then the transcript. The model comes from settings (`kiwiAgent.activeProfile`, `kiwiAgent.planProfile`), not from the UI.
11	
12	Session modes:
13	
14	- **Chat**: work in the code with the full tool set.
15	- **Plan**: blind planning of one feature. The session can read `docs/intent/**` only, enforced at the tool call, and writes `plan/<feature>.spec.md` (behaviour, invariants, edge cases, acceptance criteria, tasks, open questions, stable item ids, `status: draft`). The first prompt is the feature or user story description. Writing the spec needs no permission prompt. A bar above the transcript switches between the spec (Plan) and the conversation (Chat), shows the spec's status and has Approve; the view follows the work: Chat while the planner responds, Plan when its turn ends. Approval sets `status: approved` in the front-matter, which later phases require.
16	
17	## Develop
18	
19	```
20	npm install
21	npm test          # no network or engine needed
22	npm run build     # dist/: extension, webview, cli.mjs, ripgrep
23	```
24	
25	F5 launches the Extension Development Host. Open the "KiwiAgent" view in the activity bar.
26	
27	## Develop with it
28	
29	Load the extension from this repo in your normal VS Code instead of a packaged copy:
30	
31	```
32	npm run link-dev   # installs the .vsix so VS Code registers it, then points the installed folder at this repo
33	```
34	
35	Reload the window once. From then on, after `npm run build` (or the `npm: watch` task) the extension notices its own bundle changed and offers "Reload Window". Sessions and the open session survive the reload; engines resume on the next prompt. `npm run unlink-dev` removes the link.
36	
37	Verify-on-stop for this repo (`.vscode/settings.json`) runs typecheck, tests and build after any `.ts` edit.
38	
39	## Install elsewhere
40	
41	```
42	npm run package   # kiwi-agent-<version>.vsix
43	code --install-extension kiwi-agent-<version>.vsix
44	```
45	
46	Requires Node in the environment only if `kiwiAgent.nodePath` is set; otherwise VS Code's own executable runs the engine in Node mode.
47	
48	## Settings
49	
50	- `kiwiAgent.profiles`: engine, model, effort per profile.
51	- `kiwiAgent.activeProfile`: profile name used for new sessions; `kiwiAgent.planProfile` overrides it for plan sessions.
52	- `kiwiAgent.nodePath`: Node executable for the Claude engine; empty uses VS Code's executable.
53	- `kiwiAgent.traceEngine`: one line per Claude engine message in the KiwiAgent output channel, to see what the engine sends (thinking deltas, status) when the UI shows nothing.
54	- `kiwiAgent.verify`: commands run when the model wants to stop after editing matching files, in the directory of the nearest `project` file. Failures go back to the model and it keeps working, up to `kiwiAgent.verifyFailureBudget` consecutive failures. Default: `dotnet build` of the `.csproj` owning any edited `.cs` file. Applies to every engine.
55	- Command *KiwiAgent: Set API Key for Profile* stores keys for profiles that declare `apiKeySecret`.
56	
57	Session events are logged to `.agent/runs/<session id>/events.jsonl` in the workspace; add `.agent/` to the workspace's `.gitignore`.

# File edit diff

## Goal
A user following a session in the chat wants to see what the session did to each file without leaving the transcript. Today every edit is collapsed, so the change is invisible until it is opened. Each file edit — both the one being asked about in a permission card and the one already completed in a tool row — shows its change as a unified diff inline, kept small enough not to swallow the transcript, with a link to the whole edit for when the inline view is not enough.

## Behaviour
- B1: A completed file edit step in the transcript shows a unified diff of that edit, expanded, without the user opening anything.
- B2: A permission card for a file edit shows the same unified diff of the proposed change, in place of the raw tool arguments.
- B3: The diff shown in the chat is at most 15 lines. When the full diff is longer, the first 15 lines are shown and the remainder is omitted.
- B4: A truncated diff carries a link that states how many lines were omitted and opens the full edit.
- B5: Opening the full edit shows the pre-edit content of the file against the file as it currently stands on disk, in the editor's own diff view.
- B6: The diff is built from content captured by the extension when the edit tool call starts, not from anything the engine supplies, so it is identical on every engine and is present for edits that were auto-approved without a permission card.
- B7: A new file shows as an all-additions diff; an overwrite of an existing file shows as a diff against its prior content.
- B8: Each edit gets its own diff. Two edits to the same file in one turn are two diff blocks, each against the file as it stood before that edit.
- B9: The file path on the step is clickable and opens the file at the first changed line.
- B10: The diff shown in the chat is part of the session's transcript record, so it renders unchanged after a window reload without re-reading the file.
- B11: Context around a change is limited to three lines on each side, so the 15-line budget is spent on changed lines.

## Edge cases
- E1: The user rejects a permission card, or the edit fails → the step shows the outcome and no diff, because nothing changed.
- E2: The edit results in no change to the file → the step says so instead of showing an empty diff.
- E3: The file is opened in the full-edit view after later edits touched it → the comparison still starts from this edit's pre-edit content, so unrelated later changes appear; this is the intended reading of "the file as it is now".
- E4: The file's content cannot be read as text (binary or oversized) → the step reports the change in summary form (path and, where known, lines added and removed) with no diff and no link.
- E5: The full diff is 15 lines or fewer → it is shown whole, with no omission notice and no link.

## Tasks
- T1: Capture pre-edit content at the start of every file edit tool call and carry it on the step's transcript record, surviving reload (B6, B10).
- T2: Produce a unified diff from captured content and result, covering new file, overwrite and in-place edit, with three lines of context (B7, B8, B11, E2, E4).
- T3: Render the diff inline on completed edit steps and on edit permission cards, with the 15-line cap, the omission notice and its link (B1, B2, B3, B4, E1, E5).
- T4: Wire the link and the file path to the editor: full diff view of pre-edit content against the current file, and open-at-first-changed-line (B5, B9, E3).

## Open questions
- Q1: Should the expanded diff be collapsible again per step, and should that choice be remembered for the session?

Wrote `plan/file-edit-diff.spec.md`.

It specs inline unified diffs on both completed edit steps and edit permission cards (your Q1: both), a hard 15-line display cap with a "+N lines omitted" link into the editor's diff view, one diff per edit rather than per file (Q3), and snapshot capture at tool-call start so auto-approved edits still show a diff on either engine. Edge cases cover rejected/failed/no-op edits, binary or oversized files, and the fact that opening the full edit later shows subsequent changes too. Four tasks, and one open question: whether a step can be collapsed again and whether that sticks for the session.

Findings
F1 (contradiction, B1): every tool step in the transcript is a collapsed <details> (src/chat/webview/chat-transcript.ts, ChatTranscript.toolCall), and the product doc for this feature (docs/features/edit-diff-view.md) says a completed Edit/Write row shows the diff collapsed. B1 says expanded without the user opening anything. One of the two has to give; if B1 wins, edit rows stop behaving like every other tool row.
F2 (naive, B10/T1): the "transcript record" is the append-only event log .agent/runs/<id>/events.jsonl (src/agent/runs/run-log.ts, RunLog.append), read whole and posted to the webview on every session switch (SessionManager.transcript, ChatViewProvider.sendTranscript). Carrying the captured pre-edit content on the event means whole file contents are written per edit and re-sent to the webview on each switch. The spec should say the event carries the rendered (capped) diff plus a reference to a pre-edit snapshot stored under the run directory, with the snapshot — not the event — serving B5.
F3 (naive, B8/T2): the spec assumes one edit per tool call. The code already names the editing tools as Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit (src/agent/verify/turn-verifier.ts EDITING_TOOLS, src/agent/permissions/permission-policy.ts FILE_TOOLS, src/agent/phases/scope-guard.ts preToolUse), and chat sessions run the Claude engine with no tool restriction (src/extension.ts modeSetup, only IMPLEMENT_TOOLS/plan phases restrict), so a single MultiEdit call carries several edits and NotebookEdit edits a cell inside JSON. The spec should say which tools count as a file edit, whether a MultiEdit step is one diff for the whole call, and that NotebookEdit falls back to the summary form of E4.
F4 (naive, E2): a no-change edit is already an error, not a successful no-op: src/agent/openai-session/tools/edit.ts editTool fails on old_string === new_string and on a missing match, so that path lands in E1. The only successful no-change case is a Write of identical content (src/agent/openai-session/tools/write.ts writeTool, which writes unconditionally). E2 should name Write-with-identical-content as the case it covers.

The findings are in the spec; I need your ruling on each before I touch the items. My recommendations:

- **F1 (contradiction, B1):** rule for B1 — expanded. Your ask was explicitly that edits are "just collapsed today" and you want to see them. The doc line predates that. The 15-line cap is what makes expanded-by-default safe, so the doc's reason for collapsing is already handled. 6	# File edit diff
7	
8	## Goal
9	A user following a session in the chat wants to see what the session did to each file without leaving the transcript. Today every edit is collapsed, so the change is invisible until it is opened. Each file edit — both the one being asked about in a permission card and the one already completed in a tool row — shows its change as a unified diff inline, kept small enough not to swallow the transcript, with a link to the whole edit for when the inline view is not enough.
10	
11	## Behaviour
12	- B1: A completed file edit step in the transcript shows a unified diff of that edit, expanded, without the user opening anything.
13	- B2: A permission card for a file edit shows the same unified diff of the proposed change, in place of the raw tool arguments.
14	- B3: The diff shown in the chat is at most 15 lines. When the full diff is longer, the first 15 lines are shown and the remainder is omitted.
15	- B4: A truncated diff carries a link that states how many lines were omitted and opens the full edit.
16	- B5: Opening the full edit shows the pre-edit content of the file against the file as it currently stands on disk, in the editor's own diff view.
17	- B6: The diff is built from content captured by the extension when the edit tool call starts, not from anything the engine supplies, so it is identical on every engine and is present for edits that were auto-approved without a permission card.
18	- B7: A new file shows as an all-additions diff; an overwrite of an existing file shows as a diff against its prior content.
19	- B8: Each edit gets its own diff. Two edits to the same file in one turn are two diff blocks, each against the file as it stood before that edit.
20	- B9: The file path on the step is clickable and opens the file at the first changed line.
21	- B10: The diff shown in the chat is part of the session's transcript record, so it renders unchanged after a window reload without re-reading the file.
22	- B11: Context around a change is limited to three lines on each side, so the 15-line budget is spent on changed lines.
23	
24	## Edge cases
25	- E1: The user rejects a permission card, or the edit fails → the step shows the outcome and no diff, because nothing changed.
26	- E2: The edit results in no change to the file → the step says so instead of showing an empty diff.
27	- E3: The file is opened in the full-edit view after later edits touched it → the comparison still starts from this edit's pre-edit content, so unrelated later changes appear; this is the intended reading of "the file as it is now".
28	- E4: The file's content cannot be read as text (binary or oversized) → the step reports the change in summary form (path and, where known, lines added and removed) with no diff and no link.
29	- E5: The full diff is 15 lines or fewer → it is shown whole, with no omission notice and no link.
30	
31	## Tasks
32	- T1: Capture pre-edit content at the start of every file edit tool call and carry it on the step's transcript record, surviving reload (B6, B10).
33	- T2: Produce a unified diff from captured content and result, covering new file, overwrite and in-place edit, with three lines of context (B7, B8, B11, E2, E4).
34	- T3: Render the diff inline on completed edit steps and on edit permission cards, with the 15-line cap, the omission notice and its link (B1, B2, B3, B4, E1, E5).
35	- T4: Wire the link and the file path to the editor: full diff view of pre-edit content against the current file, and open-at-first-changed-line (B5, B9, E3).
36	
37	## Open questions
38	- Q1: Should the expanded diff be collapsible again per step, and should that choice be remembered for the session?
39	
40	## Findings
41	- F1 (contradiction, B1): every tool step in the transcript is a collapsed `<details>` (`src/chat/webview/chat-transcript.ts`, `ChatTranscript.toolCall`), and the product doc for this feature (`docs/features/edit-diff-view.md`) says a completed Edit/Write row shows the diff *collapsed*. B1 says expanded without the user opening anything. One of the two has to give; if B1 wins, edit rows stop behaving like every other tool row.
42	- F2 (naive, B10/T1): the "transcript record" is the append-only event log `.agent/runs/<id>/events.jsonl` (`src/agent/runs/run-log.ts`, `RunLog.append`), read whole and posted to the webview on every session switch (`SessionManager.transcript`, `ChatViewProvider.sendTranscript`). Carrying the captured pre-edit content on the event means whole file contents are written per edit and re-sent to the webview on each switch. The spec should say the event carries the rendered (capped) diff plus a reference to a pre-edit snapshot stored under the run directory, with the snapshot — not the event — serving B5.
43	- F3 (naive, B8/T2): the spec assumes one edit per tool call. The code already names the editing tools as `Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit` (`src/agent/verify/turn-verifier.ts` `EDITING_TOOLS`, `src/agent/permissions/permission-policy.ts` `FILE_TOOLS`, `src/agent/phases/scope-guard.ts` `preToolUse`), and chat sessions run the Claude engine with no tool restriction (`src/extension.ts` `modeSetup`, only `IMPLEMENT_TOOLS`/plan phases restrict), so a single MultiEdit call carries several edits and NotebookEdit edits a cell inside JSON. The spec should say which tools count as a file edit, whether a MultiEdit step is one diff for the whole call, and that NotebookEdit falls back to the summary form of E4.
44	- F4 (naive, E2): a no-change edit is already an error, not a successful no-op: `src/agent/openai-session/tools/edit.ts` `editTool` fails on `old_string === new_string` and on a missing match, so that path lands in E1. The only successful no-change case is a Write of identical content (`src/agent/openai-session/tools/write.ts` `writeTool`, which writes unconditionally). E2 should name Write-with-identical-content as the case it covers.
